question: Zakladateľ novodobých olympijských hier Pierre de Coubertin sám získal olympijskú zlatú medailu, hoci nebol športovec. Za čo ju dostal?
source_excerpt: The gold medal went to Georges Hohrod and M. Eschbach, purportedly of Germany, for 'Ode to Sport'; the names were a pseudonym for Pierre, Baron de Coubertin.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume Olympic medals have always been for sport only and that the founder of the Games was an organiser, not a medallist. The phrase 'he was not an athlete' gives them a foothold to reason toward the arts. The payoff is twofold: art medals really existed, and the founder won one himself.
extra.verification_notes: Coubertin won the 1912 Stockholm literature gold for 'Ode to Sport', submitted under the pseudonyms Georges Hohrod and M. Eschbach (https://www.olympedia.org/editions/6/sports/LIT).

explanation: Na prvých olympiádach sa súťažilo aj v umení a Coubertin vyhral literárnu súťaž s básňou Óda na šport. Prihlásil ju pod vymysleným menom, aby nebolo jasné, že ide o organizátora.

question: Až do roku 1920 bola olympijským športom aj disciplína, ktorú poznáte zo školských športových dní. Nepotrebujete na ňu loptu ani bránu, stačia dve družstvá a jeden hrubý povraz. O ktorú disciplínu ide?
source_excerpt: contested as a team event in the Summer Olympics at the Games of every Olympiad from 1900 to 1920.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume Olympic events are specialised elite sports. The answer is a game every Slovak knows from school sports days and company picnics, and the footholds let them work it out with an 'I can get this!' feeling.
extra.verification_notes: Tug of war was an Olympic event 1900–1920, with 1920 its last appearance, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tug_of_war_at_the_Summer_Olympics; no later return found.

explanation: Preťahovanie lanom bolo na olympiádach v rokoch 1900 až 1920. V Londýne v roku 1908 obsadili všetky tri stupne víťazov britské policajné tímy.
